message.content:
The idea of a single “best” film is inherently subjective, but there are objective markers—critical consensus, audience reception, and industry awards—that help identify the most celebrated movies of a given year. Below is a snapshot of the 2020 releases that consistently topped those metrics: | Film | Director | Key Accolades / Ratings | Notes | |------|----------|------------------------|-------| | **Nomadland** | Chloé Zhao | • 2021 Academy Award for Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actress (Frances McDormand)
• 2021 Golden Globe for Best Motion Picture – Drama
• 2021 BAFTA for Best Film
• Rotten Tomatoes: 94 % (Fresh)
• Metacritic: 88/100 | A quiet, contemplative portrait of modern American nomads that resonated with critics and audiences alike. | | **The Father** | Florian Zeller | • 2021 Academy Award for Best Actor (Anthony Hopkins)
• 2021 BAFTA for Best Actor
• Rotten Tomatoes: 95 % (Fresh)
• Metacritic: 84/100 | A psychological drama that earned praise for its storytelling and Hopkins’ performance. | | **Minari** | Lee Isaac Chung | • 2021 Academy Award nomination for Best Picture
• 2021 Golden Globe nomination for Best Motion Picture – Drama
• Rotten Tomatoes: 96 % (Fresh)
• Metacritic: 86/100 | A heartfelt family drama about Korean immigrants in rural America. | | **The Trial of the Chicago 7** | Aaron Sorkin | • 2021 Academy Award nomination for Best Picture
• 2021 Golden Globe nomination for Best Motion Picture – Drama
• Rotten Tomatoes: 93 % (Fresh)
• Metacritic: 78/100 | A courtroom drama that captured the political climate of the late 1960s. | | **Soul** | Pete Docter, Kemp Powers | • 2021 Academy Award for Best Animated Feature
• 2021 BAFTA for Best Animated Film
• Rotten Tomatoes: 98 % (Fresh)
• Metacritic: 81/100 | Pixar’s philosophical take on life and purpose, praised for animation and music. | ### How “best” is usually measured 1. **Critical Consensus** – Aggregated scores from Rotten Tomatoes (percentage of positive reviews) and Metacritic (weighted average score). 2. **Audience Reception** – CinemaScore grades, IMDb ratings, and user reviews. 3. **Industry Recognition** – Major award nominations and wins (Oscars, Golden Globes, BAFTAs, SAG Awards). 4. **Cultural Impact** – Box‑office performance, streaming viewership, and influence on public discourse. ### Why “Nomadland” often tops the list - **Critical acclaim**: It holds one of the highest Rotten Tomatoes scores among 2020 releases (94 %) and a strong Metacritic rating (88). - **Award sweep**: It won the Academy Award for Best Picture, a rare achievement for a low‑budget, independent film. - **Audience resonance**: The film’s themes of resilience and community struck a chord during a year marked by global uncertainty. ### Bottom line If you’re looking for a film that achieved the broadest critical, audience, and industry recognition in 2020, **“Nomadland”** is the most frequently cited “best” movie of that year. However, other titles like **“The Father,” “Minari,” “The Trial of the Chicago 7,”** and **“Soul”** also received top marks and are worth watching depending on your interests.
